newsitem.title: UK: International LPG weakens in Europe, sellers eye U.S.
newsitem.headline: International LPG weakens in Europe, sellers eye U.S.

text.p: International Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices continued to soften this week, with propane moving from Europe to the United States as price differentials widened, and East Asian buyers remaining sidelined as further drops are forecast.

Northwest European propane was done at 191.50 cif Germany with other delivery options in mid-week. This was around $10 a tonne below the level of the previous week, and reflects the fact that the North Sea appears well balanced during March and perhaps through April as well, according to one trader.

He added that while propane has fallen, it has remained roughly at parity with naphtha. It must go significantly below the naphtha level if it is to become attractive as an alternative cracking feedstock for petrochemical plants.

"It's not yet economical to crack it, so traditional offtake is still holding it," said the trader. But he added that with prices at Mont Belvieu in Texas at around 38.50 cents a gallon, equivalent to around $200 a tonne cif U.S. Gulf Coast, northern European levels are coming close to the level where the trans-Atlantic arbitrage is open.

Such cargoes are already moving from the Mediterranean. A major regional seller said the Mont Belvieu price netted back to around $183 fob southern Mediterranean, and cargoes are moving to the States. "It's better than selling to the north. We have to sell, there's no room for a lot of volume locally, so Mont Belvieu is best," said the seller.

There is still demand seen in the Mediterranean, especially from Spain, with bids heard from around $215 a tonne cif Spain for small lots. This is higher than the price in the main LPG centre of Lavera near Marseilles in southern France, where bids are heard coming from the low $200s a tonne on a cif basis.

But propane's fall in Europe has been fastest on the small seagoing coaster market, where trade was done on Friday at $177 a tonne fob UK South Coast for a 700 tonne piece, down more than $40 a tonne from the level of a week ago. The seller said that prices had fallen simply because supply exceeds demand for this size of cargo, and coasters have also been talked around $190 a tonne cif northwest Europe.

Butane in Europe is at a premium to propane on the cargo market, although trade has been thin. "Butane is tighter than propane so the price is higher," said a trader in Northwest Europe. It is also at a premium in the Mediterranean, where it is discussed in the range $210/215 a tonne cif Lavera, about $10 a tonne above the propane level. The exception is on the coaster market, where butane on Friday was discussed in the range $165/$175 a tonne fob Northwest Europe, up to $10 a tonne below propane.

East Asian demand remains low as buyers are still put off by the unexpectedly high level of the March Saudi Contract Price (CP), the main benchmark against which LPG trades in markets east of Suez. The CP was set at $270 a tonne for propane and $277 a tonne for butane.

"I can't see any buyers. There are potential requirements, but people are delaying," said a Japanese trader. He added that in many cases, potential buyers in South Korea, Japan and China have already deferred purchases to April where possible, and the real decision is whether to buy in April or leave it until May. Most have abandoned any idea of trying to buy in March.

As a result of the high CP, the spot price for Middle East pieces is at a discount of at least $20 a tonne to the CP, with buyers holding out for $25 a tonne below the benchmark. And in Japan, bids and offers have come down still further, with CP +$5 a tonne C+F Japan seen as a realistic price for both propane and butane.

The LPG Centre of Japan, in a regional seminar on Friday, said Asian LPG demand is expected to reach 61 million tonnes by 2000, up 51 percent from 1995 levels. In 10 countries - China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam - demand is expected to reach 32 million tonnes from 20 million tonnes over the same period. A surge in demand from China and India is seen as the major factor behind the tightening supply/demand balance.
